source: verified live on 2026-09-18: each official or fred_oecd_10y entry returned a dated observation to python/refresh_rates.py before it was recorded here
notes: Tiers: official (issuer or central bank, machine-readable) > fred_oecd_10y (OECD monthly 10y via FRED; the 7y is taken from the 10y and recorded as a substitution) > manual (hand-copied; the 45-day gate forces the refresh).
Aggregators (worldgovernmentbonds, tradingeconomics) are never a programmatic source; they are where a human reads a manual entry from.
A failed fetch writes nothing; the existing entry stays and ages out.

Nothing fetched is tracked (29): the curves themselves are written by python/refresh_rates.py to data/reference/risk_free_rates.json, gitignored, and every user runs the refresher with their own FRED key; a missing curve fails the record naming the refresher. max_age_days, tenors and aliases here seed that file.

no_curve_fallback (54): a domicile named here has no reachable official curve, and a record whose statements and price are both in one currency takes that currency's country curve for the risk-free rate while keeping the domicile's country risk premium, the risk-free parameter's source saying "trading currency; domicile curve unavailable". Uruguay is the only entry: MercadoLibre files a 10-K in dollars and trades in dollars, so the dollar curve is the rate its cash flows discount at, and no Uruguayan sovereign curve is published through any keyless source. The list is a declaration, not a fallback: a domicile not named here still fails with no risk-free curve, and a domicile named here that does have a curve takes it.

Denmark added 2026-09-24 (65): probed before it was recorded, as every official entry is. The Nationalbank's own api.nationalbanken.dk and nationalbanken.statbank.dk hosts do not resolve to a machine-readable yield table; its statistics are published through Statistics Denmark's keyless StatBank API, which returned a dated monthly observation. Mexico added 2026-09-29 (71) on the fred_oecd_10y tier, probed before it was recorded as every entry is: Banco de Mexico's SIE API needs a registered token, so the OECD monthly ten-year through FRED is the source, the seven-year substituted from it and recorded. No rate was hand-copied.

China moved from manual to official 2026-09-30 (75): the hand-copied entry, a hundred and seventeen days stale, is replaced by ChinaBond's own curve. The other manual entries were probed the same day and stay: Hong Kong's HKMA open API serves Exchange Fund Bills and Notes closing yields keyless but the notes outstanding run to three years and the Government Bond Programme datasets carry issuance and tenders, not yields; Taiwan's Taipei Exchange and stock exchange open APIs carry bond issuance and no government yield curve, and MOPS refuses scripted requests; Singapore's MAS serves its SGS yields only through its API gateway, which needs a registered credential; Kazakhstan's National Bank serves exchange rates and no yields programmatically.

China.source: ChinaBond (China Central Depository & Clearing), the China Government Bond yield curve published at yield.chinabond.com.cn, read from the chart's own endpoint
notes: The endpoint answers a form POST (locale=en_US) and nothing to a GET, with the latest day's curve as (years, per cent) pairs on a grid that carries every whole-year tenor; the curve is picked by its id, which names the China Government Bond curve (中债国债收益率曲线); verified 2026-09-30, a dated curve came back to python/refresh_rates.py before this entry was written.
as_of is the day the curve is for (worktime), a daily observation.
FRED carries no OECD series for China.

No programmatic source reachable. Refresh by hand from MAS SGS prices and yields: edit the country's entry in risk_free_rates.json, set as_of to the quote date, keep estimated on interpolated tenors. MAS publishes no 3-year benchmark and discontinued the 7-year on 1 February 2011, so those two tenors are interpolated on every vintage.

Probed again on 2026-09-23 (54) and every route refused: the eservices datastore API answers with MAS's failover maintenance page, as it did on 2026-09-18; the eservices statistics REST API serves the bond and bill auction results and the savings-bond table but has no yields endpoint; the Financial Database Application's benchmark prices and yields page is an ASP.NET form whose postback returns the same maintenance notice and which offers no JSON or CSV route; data.gov.sg carries no yield dataset among its whole catalogue; and FRED carries no Singapore government bond series at all. The entry stays manual until MAS's statistics service returns.

Denmark.source: Danmarks Nationalbank, ten-year central government bond redemption yield (monthly average), served keyless through Statistics Denmark's StatBank, table MPK3, series type 5500701004
notes: Danmarks Nationalbank's own StatBank states that its subject areas are served as part of Statistics Denmark's StatBank, which is why the host is api.statbank.dk and no Nationalbank host is used; verified 2026-09-24, a dated observation came back before this entry was written.

MPK3 carries no tenor shorter than ten years and the Nationalbank's daily table DNRENTD carries policy and reference rates only, not bond yields, so the seven-year is substituted from the ten-year and recorded, as the OECD monthly tier does.
as_of is the end of the observation month, the point at which the monthly average is complete.
The time filter is an open lower bound well in the past, so the URL never needs editing; the parser takes the newest period the response carries.
